newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Third Australian dies under voluntary euthanasia law.
newsitem.headline: Third Australian dies under voluntary euthanasia law.

text.p: A third Australian, a 69-year old man, has committed suicide using a computerised lethal injection system under the ethanasia laws of the Northern Territory, a enthanasia supporters group said on Wednesday.
The National Coalition for Voluntary Ethanasia said on its Internet site that the man, who was not identified, had been suffering from terminal stomach cancer and died on Monday.
The man is the third person to die under the world's first euthanasia law, which came into force in the Territory in July.
In September, 66-year old cancer patient Bob Dent became the first person to use the legislation to die. Janet Mills, 52 and also a cancer sufferer, took her life on January 2.
"The patient thanked those who made it possible for him to use the Act ..." Dr Robert Marr of the Coalition for Voluntary Euthanasia said on the Internet page Deliverance.
"The specialist was very happy to sign the form and all the safeguards have been met and it shows the law is working well," he said on Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
An alliance of church and civic leaders are leading a legal and parliamentary battle to quash the Territory's Rights of the Terminally Ill Act.
